title: Which page has longer sentences?
description: Two pages of text are compared by counting the words in each sentence. The mean and median of the sentence lengths are found for each page and used to describe which page has longer sentences.
teaching_notes: One idea: the mean and median of sentence lengths describe a page, and pages with a different number of sentences can still be compared. Watch for children who compare the total words on the two pages.

video_script.why: The child can find a mean and a median and now collects data from text.
video_script.substitution: Counting the words in each sentence turns a page of text into a list of numbers.
video_script.anchor: Sample sentence lengths in words. First page: 12, 8, 15, 20, 9, 14, 11, 7. Second page: 18, 22, 25, 14, 30, 19.
video_script.payoff_line: The second page has longer and more varied sentences.

final_answer.value: For the sample pages: page A mean 12, median 11.5; page B mean ≈ 21.33, median 20.5
final_answer.spoken: the second page has longer and more varied sentences

maths_rules: sample data, labelled sample: first set 12, 8, 15, 20, 9, 14, 11, 7; second set 18, 22, 25, 14, 30, 19
gaps from shortest to longest: 20 - 7 = 13 and 30 - 14 = 16
check: first page has 4 sentences below 11.5 and 4 above; second page has 3 below 20.5 and 3 above
with your own pages: collect, sort, compute, plot and compare
video_script.design: Two pages of text, each with its sentences turned into numbers, and one dot plot line shared by both.
open_questions: The book asks the viewer to choose a project and a page, so the two lists of sentence lengths are sample data from the worklist, labelled sample on screen. Only the sentence-length project is shown, not the project about names.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Count the words in each sentence to get a list of numbers.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The total divided by the number of sentences is called the mean.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The middle of the sorted list is called the median.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, draw the dot plot. Use one number line from five to thirty.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, find the mean and median of the first page. The eight numbers add up to ninety six.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ninety six divided by eight is twelve.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Sort the numbers. With eight values, the median is halfway between the fourth and fifth values. Those are eleven and twelve.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Half of twenty three is eleven point five.

marks.m1: the six numbers are added and 128 is written
marks.m3: the numbers are sorted and the third and fourth glow

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, find the mean and median of the second page. The six numbers add up to one hundred and twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One hundred and twenty eight divided by six is about twenty one point three three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Sort the numbers. With six values, the median is halfway between the third and fourth values. Those are nineteen and twenty two.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Half of forty one is twenty point five.
